content:
sara: opened a docs PR that adds a Windows & IPv6 appendix for Private/VPC installs. Covers HSM PKCS#11 on Windows (where applicable), Windows service example, notes for WSL/ARM64, and an IPv6 firewall checklist. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/1724

tom: skimmed. love the Windows coverage. two quick asks: 1) show an example for creating a Windows service for kms-proxy (sc.exe or NSSM), 2) call out that many HSM vendors expose a named pipe or sysfs-like socket differently on Windows — include vendor-specific note placeholder.

keiko: I can add the NSSM example and a short WSL note. For NSSM: `nssm install kms-proxy \"C:\\Program Files\\redwood\\kms-proxy.exe\" \"--config\" \"C:\\etc\\redwood\\kms-proxy.yaml\"` and set service user to a local svc account. Will also add an alt-texted diagram under assets/diagrams/windows-topology.svg and reference it as `../assets/diagrams/windows-topology.svg`.

jon: IPv6 checklist: add ip6tables / Windows Firewall rule examples. Example Windows PowerShell snippet: `New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName \"Allow KMS TLS\" -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 443 -Action Allow -Profile Any` and for ip6tables: `ip6tables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT`. Also mention dual-stack SNI considerations when customers use TLS with IPv6 addresses.

sara: good. can we also add a short note about unix socket vs named pipe endpoints in SDK examples? Node and Python clients sometimes choke on `unix://` URIs on Windows. Suggest showing both `unix://` (Linux) and `npipe://` or `file:` alternatives for Windows.

tom: yes — Node example to add:```js
// unix socket (Linux)
const client = new KmsClient({ endpoint: 'unix:///var/run/hsm/pkcs11.sock' });
// windows named pipe example (vendor-specific)
const clientWin = new KmsClient({ endpoint: 'npipe:////./pipe/hsm-pkcs11' });
```

keiko: WSL/ARM note: if running kms-proxy under WSL2, sockets live in the WSL filesystem; recommend using a Linux build for onprem ARM64 or containers. I'll add: \"For ARM64 Windows hosts, prefer containerized kms-proxy on Linux/ARM image when possible; test HSM vendor support.\"

jon: small security note: Windows file ACL example to allow service account access to a named pipe or socket equivalent — include PowerShell `Set-Acl` snippet and recommend minimizing permissions.

docs-bot: lint: link-check OK, spelling: 1 warning (\"priviledged\" -> \"privileged\"), accessibility: svg alt missing in initial commit (keiko has alt fix pending). CI preview: https://deploy-preview-1724--docs.redwood.ai/private-windows-ipv6-appendix

sara: keiko can you paste the NSSM + PowerShell ACL snippet into the PR? Also add a short troubleshooting section referencing `Get-Service kms-proxy`, Event Viewer for service failures, and `netstat -an -p tcp` / `ss -xl` depending on platform.

keiko: added NSSM example and PowerShell ACL snippet:```powershell
# Install service with NSSM
nssm install kms-proxy \"C:\\Program Files\\redwood\\kms-proxy.exe\" \"--config\" \"C:\\etc\\redwood\\kms-proxy.yaml\"
# Grant service account read access to cert bundle
$acl = Get-Acl \"C:\\etc\\redwood\\certs\\kms-bundle.pem\"
$rule = New-Object System.Security.AccessControl.FileSystemAccessRule(\"NT Service\\kms\",\"Read\",\"Allow\")
$acl.AddAccessRule($rule)
Set-Acl \"C:\\etc\\redwood\\certs\\kms-bundle.pem\" $acl
```
Also added Event Viewer + `Get-WinEvent -LogName Application -MaxEvents 50` troubleshooting bullet. Pushed commit and updated SVG alt text.

tom: ACK. one more SDK nit: include a short Go example showing env-based endpoint for cross-platform:```go
endpoint := os.Getenv("KMS_ENDPOINT") // unix:///... or npipe:////./pipe/...
conn, err := grpc.Dial(endpoint, grpc.WithTransportCredentials(creds))
```

sara: perfect. If no more objections I'll merge after CI. keiko/tom can you follow up with any vendor-specific HSM notes in a follow-up PR (we left placeholders).

docs-bot: final lint (after pushes): link-check OK, spelling fixed, accessibility OK. Preview: https://deploy-preview-1724--docs.redwood.ai/private-windows-ipv6-appendix

keiko: LGTM, merging in 5m unless anyone objects. thanks all :white_check_mark:
